### G-C2 — Operator-Coupled KV Rounding (K co-monotone shared-threshold rounding, V weighted dependent rounding)
- **Intuition**: When writing a 128-token KV block to a low-bit cache, decide the rounding directions of different tokens jointly instead of independently, with different correlation structures for K and V because they play different roles in softmax(QK^T/sqrt d)V. This lets the cache use fewer bits (first target: K2/V2 -> K2/V1) at the same task quality, so freed memory becomes higher concurrency and lower wall-clock time per correct answer on 16K-64K long-CoT decoding.
- **K: co-monotone shared-threshold rounding**: within a block, for the same KV head and the same coordinate, use one shared U ~ Uniform(0,1) and round token i up iff U < f_i, where f_i is the element's fractional position between adjacent grid points. Goal: make K errors of different tokens positively correlated, so the perturbation of the score distribution (softmax is shift-invariant) is reduced.
- **V: weighted dependent rounding**: x_i = (v_i - l_i)/Delta_i. Pair two not-yet-rounded variables; alpha = min{Delta_i(1-x_i), Delta_j x_j}, beta = min{Delta_i x_i, Delta_j(1-x_j)}; update x_i <- x_i + t/Delta_i, x_j <- x_j - t/Delta_j with t = alpha w.p. beta/(alpha+beta), t = -beta w.p. alpha/(alpha+beta). This keeps each marginal's expectation and preserves the Delta-weighted sum (the dequantized sum) of the block, giving negatively correlated V errors.
- **Relation to existing quantizers**: reuses an existing quantizer's grid (Hadamard rotation, variance normalization, scales, zero points, clipping, packed format, e.g. KVarN); only the write-time rounding rule changes; no persistent side code.
- **Claimed local theory**: (K) for fixed post-RoPE K, fixed query and fixed grid, the expected forward-KL of attention under shared-threshold coupling is no larger than under independent stochastic rounding with the same marginals. (V) for fixed nonnegative attention weights and independent V randomness across blocks, the weighted readout error variance is no larger than under independent rounding. The candidate states these do not imply unchanged autoregressive generation, accuracy or length.
- **Claimed novelty**: separate error-correlation design for K and V; moving dependent rounding from budget allocation onto actual KV numeric grids; no extra side code; lower bit width converted into higher concurrency and lower cost per solved problem.
- **Baselines (as claimed)**: BF16, FP8, KIVI-2, KVarN, PM-KVQ, R-KV, TurboQuant (with/without boundary-layer protection), ThinKV, TaSQ, Spend Bytes on Breadth, random (stochastic) rounding, round-to-nearest, deterministic residual feedback. Ablations: K-only, V-only, full K+V, weighted vs unweighted V rounding.
- **Evaluation**: stage 1 Qwen3-8B, AIME25 and MATH-500, 2/3/4 bit; accuracy, CTIR, length distribution, loop rate, length-cap rate, peak memory, batch saturation, wall-clock per correct answer. Stage 2 Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507, R1-Distill-Qwen-14B/32B, gpt-oss-20b; AIME 2026, GPQA-Diamond, LiveCodeBench; AIME avg@16.
- **Kill test (as claimed)**: week 1 on Qwen3-8B with FP8, KVarN, PM-KVQ, TurboQuant baselines in vLLM; compare RTN, independent SR, K-only, V-only, full C2. Stop if C2 beats only independent SR but not RTN/KVarN on the real quality-cost frontier; drop the K+V version if V-only explains all gains; drop K2/V1 if it fails accuracy, length and service-time requirements.
